primitive.relation: definitional equality: X157's and X164's local decoders x157_data_nth_nat / x164_data_nth_nat d i (identical bodies) are GTBase.complexity.data_nth_nat d i, the same fixpoint, with every corner kept: position 0 of a Dcons cell is its head's natural value (0 for a non-Dnat head), position j+1 recurses into the tail, a scalar Dnat n (whole datum or malformed tail) reads n at its position 0 and 0 after, Dnil and Dpair read 0 everywhere. The colour adapters (x157_output_colour modulo k, x164_output_colour modulo 3, both at the vertex's enum rank) stay distinct and unchanged.

positional-natural-decoder.note: data_nth_nat d i: the natural at position i read through Dcons cells; a non-natural entry, a position past the end, Dnil and Dpair read 0; a scalar Dnat n reads n at its position 0, also as a malformed tail (data_nth_nat0, data_nth_natS); on an encoded list of naturals it is nth 0 (data_nth_nat_enc_list, data_nth_nat_enc_list_default).

upstream_audit.note: The complexity model's data type, its encoders (enc_list, enc_nat) and the scalar reader data_nat_value are GTBase's own (GTBase.complexity); neither MathComp nor the pinned GraphTheory knows this data type, and GTBase.complexity has no positional reader before this family (data_nat_value reads a single Dnat only). MathComp's nth is the reference behaviour on encoded lists (data_nth_nat_enc_list), not a candidate for the data type itself. So the decoder is added to GTBase.complexity, next to data_nat_value, with the legacy body unchanged.
